measurements: Probe cost, measured on 8692234+ code (the head) with a source that logs every read. It counts only PaddingAt's eightfold windows at the named offset, which the table's window and the rebuild's read after. Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-AdCodicem-Pdf/b5ddd9fc-0507-5e11-8a94-c9e1fedd4860/scratchpad/lot19/r5b/ZzR5bProbeCostTests.cs.txt; output: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-AdCodicem-Pdf/b5ddd9fc-0507-5e11-8a94-c9e1fedd4860/scratchpad/lot19/r5b/probe-cost.txt. The ratio is probe bytes over the bytes from the offset to the first token's end, capped at the probe's reach (MaxTrailerLength + 32).

28 spaces + xref (keyword ending on byte 32): windows [32,256] = 288 bytes, 9.00 times the 32 bytes to the token's end (10.29 times the run alone, the old remark's failure). 29 spaces: 8.73. 27 spaces: one probe of 32.
1, 2 and 3 spaces + xref: one 32-byte probe each, the token ending within the first probe (6.40, 5.33 and 4.57 times; 32, 16 and 10.67 times the run alone). The remark's one-probe clause covers this.

Long first token, no white space: a 70,000-byte name reads [32,256,2048,16384,65568] = 84,288 bytes, 1.29 times the 65,568 counted to the probe's reach. With 1 space before it, or a 69,002-byte string, the result is the same. A 40-byte name: [32,256] = 288, 7.20. A 300-byte name: [32,256,2048] = 2,336, 7.79. Headers: 25 spaces + '1234567890 0 obj' reads 288, 7.02; 12 spaces + a 20-digit number reads 288, 7.58.

Runs past 16 KiB: 16,385 spaces + xref reads 84,288 (5.14 times); 20,000 reads 4.21; 60,000 reads 1.40; 65,536 reads 1.29; 70,000 (guard) reads 84,288 against the 65,568 reach, 1.29. Worst case overall: 2,044 spaces + xref, the keyword ending on the 2,048-byte edge, reads [32,256,2048,16384] = 18,720, 9.14 times (64/7). 2,048 spaces reads 9.12. A 100-byte comment + xref reads 288, 2.77.

Lowered bounds: at 256, 257 spaces reads [32,256,288], 2.21, and 300 spaces reads 2.00; at 1, 40 spaces reads [32,33], 1.97. Probe bytes over the last window reach 1.286 under the default cap (84,288 / 65,568), which confirms that the old 'a seventh more than the last window' wording was false and was not restored.

Conclusion: every shape with more than one probe stays under ten times (at most 9.14). One probe is read wherever the first token ends short of the first probe's edge. The new remark's bound holds in every case measured, the cap included.

Checked the threshold against the code: with whole reads the search ends at the end of line before the keyword. Short reads of 11 bytes or more do the same: 11 steps 1 byte and still repeats the full 10-byte overlap, 12 steps 2, 40 steps 30. A 10-byte read repeats 9 bytes, so the CR of a CRLF is lost. A 9-byte read repeats 8, so the whole end of line is lost. A read shorter than 9 never holds the keyword whole. This matches the refuter's probe output (zz-r5-endstream-short.txt).

deviations: StreamEnds.cs: the task's text was '... or the read before held no more bytes than the overlap, which only a source that gives fewer bytes than asked may do before the end of the file (#52)'. I wrote '... or the read before was a window of the file that held no more bytes than the overlap, which only a source that gives fewer bytes than asked may lend before the end of the file (#52)'. Reason: StreamEnds calls the parser's bytes a read too. Those bytes can hold 10 or fewer data bytes without any short source, after a dictionary that nearly fills the 8 KB window. In that case the first window starts at the data's start (position = dataStart + max(0, buffered - 10)), so no end of line is lost. The task's wording would be false for that read; naming the window of the file keeps it exact.

HeaderText.HeaderAt: the parameter keyword is renamed tokenStart. The task allowed a rename if it reads better and nothing else changes; the one call passes it by position. The whole text stays in the <summary>, as the task asked, not split into remarks.

docs/threat-model.md: the #52 known-gap entry (:366-372) now says the endstream search may miss a keyword, a header or the end of line 'after a read of no more bytes than the ten its reads repeat', and that 'a read of more, short or not, leaves the search as whole reads leave it'. The task did not name this entry, but it describes the same mechanism the corrected remarks state, and the stage brief allows updating the threat-model rows that describe what the stage changes. R5d's #331 split works on the same entry and should keep this clause.

The theory places the endstream 30 to 59 bytes past the parser's window rather than at 20,000 bytes as in the refuter's probe. This keeps each capped search to tens of reads rather than about 12,000, while still giving every alignment for steps 1, 2 and 30. It reuses HeaderFile and HeaderEnding with header = end of line + 'endstream\nendobj\n12 0 obj', so the file holds a well-formed object 12 after object 5. Object 6 is padded to TailSearchLength so the startxref read lies past the capped reads.
